items.title: Somalia: Doolow Explosions Trigger Clash of Accounts Between Jubbaland and Mogadishu
items.description: Jubbaland said General Abdirahman and members of his family were inside the residence when the explosions occurred, sustaining minor injuries before being moved to a secure location for treatment. The Somali federal government, however, has denied any involvement in the incident and offered a different account. Government officials said preliminary information gathered by security agencies indicates that the explosions were caused by materials being prepared inside the house, rather than by an external airstrike. The government's account could not immediately be independently verified. Jubbala
items.titleIt: Somalia: Doolow Explosions Trigger Clash of Accounts Between Jubbaland and Mogadishu

items.title: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt being flown back to Italy - Tajani
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 3 - A six-year-old boy who has been in a coma in an Egyptian hospital since an August 3 accident at a swimming pool at Sharm El Sheikh is currently being flown back to Italy, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on a visit to Cairo Thursday. The boy, Younes Majidi, who suffered a cardiac arrest and has been in critical condition since nearly drowning at the Red Sea resort, will be admitted for treatment at the Regina Margherita Children's Hospital in Turin, said Tajani, who is also deputy premier. (ANSA). Read article...
items.titleIt: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt being flown back to Italy - Tajani

items.title: Somalia: How Sadia Bajaaj Was Convicted — Inside the Judge Swap and the Pressure Behind Her Case
items.description: According to her legal team and a review of court proceedings, a judge was swapped out mid-trial, and the Attorney General's office pushed the case at both the trial and the appeal. A Conviction That Almost Didn't Happen Sadia, a tuk-tuk driver turned social media activist, was arrested twice in 2026. items.titleIt: Somalia: How Sadia Bajaaj Was Convicted — Inside the Judge Swap and the Pressure Behind Her Case

items.title: Meloni govt to extend 17-cent cut in diesel duties to Sept 10
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 04 SET - The economy ministry has prepared a decree extending a 17-cent cut in diesel duties until September 10, sources said on Friday. The cut was first introduced by Premier Giorgia Meloni's government at the end of July to help people cope with high fuel costs following the return of conflict in the Persian Gulf and it has been renewed several times since. The current reduction was set to expire on Saturday. The cut, which does not regard unleaded petrol, has not stopped diesel prices from rising well above two euros a litre. The centre-left opposition has criticised the cut
items.titleIt: Meloni govt to extend 17-cent cut in diesel duties to Sept 10

items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 3 - Italian pasta giant Barilla said Thursday that it has reached an agreement to buy Goodles, an American macaroni-and-cheese brand, confirming a report in The Wall Street Journal. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.
items.titleIt: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran

items.title: Egypt: Cairo and Beijing sign deals on economy, technology
items.description: On Wednesday, Xi Jinping and his Egyptian counterpart, president Abdel Fatah el-Sissi, oversaw the signing of a series of deals, including on technology, economic co operation and the digital economy.
items.titleIt: Egypt: Cairo and Beijing sign deals on economy, technology

items.title: Chinese President Xi starts state visit to Egypt with energy, AI on agenda
items.description: The leaders are expected to sign agreements on artificial intelligence, transport, energy and investment in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, Egyptian media reported
items.titleIt: Chinese President Xi starts state visit to Egypt with energy, AI on agenda

items.title: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Connects Climate Solutions From Field To Factory
items.description: [Bird Story Agency] As rainfall becomes less predictable, researchers are developing improved seed, testing more efficient irrigation and using digital tools to track water losses. Getting these solutions to farmers could protect harvests and provide Ethiopia's textile factories with more locally grown fibre.
items.titleIt: Ethiopia: Ethiopia Connects Climate Solutions From Field To Factory

items.title: Kenya: Kuria Warns Kenya Will Fall Behind Uganda, Tanzania Unless It Changes Industrialisation Policy
items.description: [Capital FM] Nairobi -- Former Investments, Trade and Industry Cabinet Secretary Moses Kuria has backed the Government's decision to push Tata Chemicals Magadi out of Kenya, arguing that the country risks being overtaken by Uganda, Ethiopia, Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of Congo unless it fundamentally changes how it exploits its natural resources.
items.titleIt: Kenya: Kuria Warns Kenya Will Fall Behind Uganda, Tanzania Unless It Changes Industrialisation Policy

items.title: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt being flown back to Italy - Tajani
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, SEP 3 - A six-year-old boy who has been in a coma in an Egyptian hospital since an August 3 accident at a swimming pool at Sharm El Sheikh is currently being flown back to Italy, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on a visit to Cairo Thursday. The boy, Younes Majidi, who suffered a cardiac arrest and has been in critical condition since nearly drowning at the Red Sea resort, will be admitted for treatment at the Regina Margherita Children's Hospital in Turin, said Tajani, who is also deputy premier. (ANSA). Read article...
items.titleIt: Boy, 6, in coma after pool accident in Egypt being flown back to Italy - Tajani

items.description: Several Egyptian officials have hailed Chinese President Xi Jinping's latest state visit to their country as a boost to bilateral relations and a tour that could add stability to a world with rising regional and international tensions.

items.title: Tajani meets Sisi, set to sign agreement with Egypt on migrants

items.title: IPI: Africa Media Freedom Monitoring: April to June 2026
items.description: The International Press Institute (IPI) recorded nearly 100 cases of threats and attacks on journalists (82 male and 18 female) across 22 countries in sub-Saharan Africa between April and June 2026. Physical and verbal attacks, as well as arrests and detention, were the most frequent types of incidents. An Ethiopian journalist in exile was found dead in Kenya under suspicious circumstances.   Police and state security forces (55%) continued to be the primary perpetrators of attacks and threats against journalists, a trend that continues from the previous quarter.
